title: Derived self-Tor charts and comparisons for fixed quotient resolutions
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion and n≥0. Let B=i_*O_Z and Q=i^*H^(-n)(B[0]⊗ᴸB[0]) for the fixed derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For every affine U set A_U=Γ(Y,U), I_U=ker(i)(U), M_U=Tor⁽ᴬᵁ⁾ₙ(A_U/I_U,A_U/I_U) [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], and let P_U be Mathlib’s projectiveResolution of A_U/I_U. Let T_U be tilde followed by affine chart restriction, pushforward to Y and tensor pullback to Z. There is a family t_U:T_U(M_U)|i⁻¹U≅Q|i⁻¹U. For every affine principal inclusion V⊆U there exist a quotient ring map ψ compatible with the structure sheaf restriction, an augmented chain map a:P_U→Res(P_V), and a quotient tensor chain map k carrying x⊗y to a(x)⊗ψ(y). Let q:M_U→M_V be the explicitly constructed function obtained by composing the P_U Tor-to-homology isomorphism, H_n(k), the exact restriction-of-scalars homology isomorphism, and the inverse P_V Tor-to-homology isomorphism. Then t_U on the restriction of selfTorAffineSection_U(x) equals t_V on selfTorAffineSection_V(q(x)) for every x [new-t2-self-tor-affine-section]. Only the fixed P_U,P_V and their augmented tensor chain comparisons are involved. Neither a cycle formula nor a universal certificate is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the augmented geometric comparison to obtain the family t and its compatibility for every given augmented comparison.

On the basic inclusion, apply the quotient-resolution tensor comparison to obtain ψ, a and k, using the ideal containment supplied by the ideal sheaf restriction. Feed these data to the geometric compatibility statement.
